cards.text: Isaiah, God's prophet, has just shared the LORD's promise to gather people from all the nations to His house of prayer (Isaiah 56:7-8). Then the message turns: a call goes out to all the beasts of the field and the forest to come and eat greedily. Next up are Israel's watchmen, and a watchman's whole job is to see trouble coming.

cards.question: Israel's watchmen should be the first to see trouble coming, but they are all ___.
True or false: Israel's watchmen are pictured as watchdogs that bark at every danger.

cards.text: They're mute dogs that can't bark, dreamers lying around who love to slumber. A watchdog that can't bark is a smoke detector with the batteries pulled out: looks GREAT on the ceiling, does NOTHING in a fire.
Then the dogs get hungry. This same crew is like ravenous dogs that are never satisfied, and they're shepherds too, the ones meant to guide God's people.

cards.question: Israel's shepherds have no ___, and they all turn to their own way.
Shepherds are supposed to care for the flock. What is each of these shepherds seeking instead?

cards.text: And these shepherds have a party plan. They call for wine and strong drink.

cards.question: Israel's shepherds call for wine and strong drink. How do they picture tomorrow?

cards.text: Meanwhile, the righteous perish, and no one takes it to heart. Devout men are taken away too, and no one stops to consider what that really means for them.

cards.question: When devout men are taken away, what does no one stop to consider?

answers.text: They are taken from the presence of evil
They are punished for hidden sins

cards.question: True or false: Those who walk uprightly find no rest, even in death.

cards.text: Now God calls a group forward, and He doesn't hold back: "But come here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes!" Then He asks who they think they're mocking, sneering at and sticking their tongues out at.

cards.question: True or false: God calls these mockers children of transgression and offspring of deceit.

cards.text: God says they burn with lust among the oaks and under every luxuriant tree, and they slaughter their children in the valleys. They've even poured out drink offerings and grain offerings to the smooth stones of the valley.

cards.question: After all those offerings poured out to the smooth stones of the valley, what does God ask?

answers.text: Should I relent because of these
Who taught you to do these things
When will you return to Me

cards.text: Then God says they made their bed on a high and lofty hill, and that's where they went up to offer sacrifices.

cards.question: God tells them that in all of this, they were ___ Him.

cards.text: They made a pact with those whose bed they loved. And they went to Molech, a false god of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11:7), with oil and more and more perfume.

cards.question: God says they sent their envoys a great distance. How far down did they go?

cards.text: All those journeys wear them out.

cards.question: True or false: Worn out from their many journeys, they finally said there is no hope.

cards.text: Nope, they found renewal of their strength, so they didn't grow weak. That's me, lost on the highway for three hours with the gas light on, STILL saying, "Nah, I know exactly where I'm going."
Then God asks whom they've dreaded and feared so much that they lied and failed to remember Him.

cards.question: God asks a question about why they don't fear Him. What reason does He raise?

cards.text: God says He will expose their righteousness and their works, and none of it will profit them.

cards.question: When they cry out, God tells them to let their companies of ___ deliver them.
True or false: A breath of wind is enough to take all those idols away.
Unlike those who trust in idols, who will inherit the land and possess God's holy mountain?

answers.text: Whoever was born in the land

cards.text: Then the tone shifts. It will be said, "Build it up, build it up, prepare the way, take every obstacle out of the way of My people."
And the One who is high and lifted up, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, speaks. He says He dwells in a high and holy place.

cards.question: Besides the high and holy place, who does the Holy One say He dwells with?

answers.text: The oppressed and humble in spirit
The mighty and wise in heart
The priests who serve at His altar

cards.question: True or false: The Holy One dwells with the humble to revive the heart of the contrite.

cards.text: He's there to restore the spirit of the lowly too. Friend, I spent years at the back of a junk drawer under old takeout menus, so trust me, NOBODY knows lowly like I know lowly.
God says He will not accuse forever, nor will He always be angry.

cards.question: God says He won't be angry forever. What reason does He give?

answers.text: Man's spirit would grow weak before Him
His people have paid for their sins
His anger fades with the years

cards.text: God says He was enraged by "his sinful greed," so He struck him and hid His face in anger.

cards.question: True or false: Even after God struck him for his sinful greed, he kept turning back to the desires of his heart.
God has seen the ways of the one whose sinful greed angered Him, and still He says He will ___ him.

cards.text: God says He'll guide him and restore comfort to him and his mourners, bringing praise to their lips.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD speaks peace only to those who are near.

cards.text: But then comes a hard contrast. The wicked are like the storm-tossed sea.

cards.question: The wicked are like the storm-tossed sea. What can that sea never do?

cards.text: Its waves churn up mire and muck. That's my brain at 3 a.m., replaying something dumb I said to a mixing bowl twenty years ago.

cards.question: The prophet closes with the words of his God: there is no ___ for the wicked.

findings.problem: Nothing before this blank sets up the idea of discernment, so 'shepherds with no ___' is close to guessing a word from the line. 'strength' and 'flock' fit the sentence just as easily, and only luck or the bare hint 'turn to their own way' points to 'discernment.'

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has three things happening: burning with lust among the oaks, slaughtering children in the valleys, and offerings to the smooth stones. Split it.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Isaiah 57:6 says 'you have poured out a drink offering and offered a grain offering.' The card makes both plural ('drink offerings and grain offerings') and says both were 'poured out,' but the text says only the drink offering was poured.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'In all of this, they were ___ Him' ties 'Forsaking Me' to everything they've done. In Isaiah 57:8, 'Forsaking Me' goes with uncovering the bed. The card states a connection the text doesn't. Ask about the line where it sits, without 'in all of this.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'That's me, lost on the highway for three hours with the gas light on' puts Papa Dorin behind the wheel of a car. That is a new event in his own story, outside the Millers' kitchen, the drawer and the Dorinverse, and not a small moment around his bakery. Make the everyday scenario a made-up one about someone else, or keep the self-joke inside his own world.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Many story cards are flat retellings with none of Papa Dorin's voice, like a plain summary of the verse: stop 1 card 8; stop 2 cards 5, 9, 12 and 14; stop 3 cards 2, 6, 11 and 13. Only four cards in the whole walkthrough carry a laugh. Stop 2's dark material needs a lighter touch, but stops 1 and 3 have room for his reactions, his disbelief and his storyteller rhythm without muddying a fact.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
